# Can one permanent tissue do every job?

<!-- STEP id="jobs" -->
## Many jobs in one plant
A plant has to do many jobs at the same time:

- cover its surface, protect it and reduce water loss
- take in water and minerals from the soil
- carry water up, and carry food to every part
- store food
- hold up its stem and leaves

<!-- STEP id="cells" -->
## Different jobs, different cells
A cell that carries water is long and tube-shaped, while a cell that stores food is soft and has room inside for the food. One kind of cell cannot be both at the same time.

**So one permanent tissue cannot do every job.**

<!-- STEP id="next" -->
> In the next lesson, you will look inside a sunflower stem. How many kinds of permanent tissue will you find there, and what does each one do?
